subject: Zephyr Data — latency & error surge RCA, remediation runbook, ownership matrix
messages:
From: Chris Barnes <chris@zephyrdata.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: support@zephyrdata.com
Date: 2027-01-19T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Spike impacting API tail latency and 5xxs — immediate follow-up

Grace —

Thanks again for the quick support this morning. We saw a big spike starting ~06:40 PST where 99.9th pct latency shot up and a subset of ingestion calls returned 500s for ~18 minutes. Our SREs traced a backlog in your zephyr-us-west node pool; it impacted two customer-critical flows.

We need an RCA and a remediation plan that covers: root cause, why autoscaling didn’t prevent the backlog, short-term mitigations for us, and longer-term actions with owners and expected delivery dates. Our execs want a readout by EOD Friday.

Can you confirm when we’ll have the initial RCA and who will own follow-through?

Chris
Senior Platform Ops — Zephyr Data

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: Chris Barnes <chris@zephyrdata.com>, support@zephyrdata.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-01-19T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Spike impacting API tail latency and 5xxs — immediate follow-up

Chris —

Appreciate the details and flag. We’re assembling the incident packet now. Short answers up front:
- ETA for initial RCA (summary + timeline): 48 hours (will share a one-page exec summary within 24 hrs)
- Short-term mitigation: temporary request routing to standby pool and KV-cache priming (already applied at 08:56 PST)
- Owners: Rishi (runtime), Laura (customer comms), Marcus (capacity/autoscale tuning)

I’ll drop the one‑page exec summary to this thread this afternoon and the full RCA + remediation runbook by Friday. Laura will coordinate an ops-level call with your SREs to align runbook steps.

Grace O'Connor

Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, Chris Barnes <chris@zephyrdata.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-01-20T11:22:00-08:00
Subject: RCA (draft) — Zephyr us-west throughput/latency spike

Attached is the draft RCA and a remediation runbook (attachments). Executive summary:
- Incident window: 2027-01-19T06:39–06:57 PST (18 min) with elevated 5xx rate peaking 06:47–06:50.
- Root cause (high level): sudden shift in request fanout pattern from Zephyr ingestion path plus correlated pause in leader election housekeeping on the inference controller; together these caused request queue growth on zephyr-us-west pool and KV cache misses that amplified latency.
- Why autoscale didn’t absorb: our autoscaler evaluates GPU utilization and request queue length with a 1m smoothing window; the surge concentrated at the tail and created head-of-line blocking on a small subset of shards before utilization signal crossed scale threshold.

Action highlights (short term):
1) Immediate: route Zephyr ingestion traffic to standby pool in us-west during peak windows (implemented 2027-01-19 08:56 PST).
2) Guard: reduce autoscale smoothing to 20s for small shard pools and add request-queue alerts at 5s median request latency.
3) Cache: implement proactive KV warmup for known ingestion prefixes.

Owners and target dates (draft):
- Rishi M. — autoscale smoothing change + alerts; target 2027-01-25
- Marcus L. — standby pool capacity + routing policy; target 2027-01-21
- Evelyn H. — regression tests & evals for leader election pause; target 2027-02-02

Attachments: zephyr_rca_v1.pdf, remediation_runbook.xlsx (detailed steps + playbook), ownership_matrix.csv (owners + SLAs).

Please review and call out any corrections. I’ll sync with Marcus to lock the standby pool sizes today.

—Rishi
Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Chris Barnes <chris@zephyrdata.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-01-20T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RCA (draft) — Zephyr us-west throughput/latency spike

Rishi/Grace —

Thanks for the speedy draft. A couple of asks from our SRE side:
- Can you show the specific shard ids and request examples that produced the worst tail behavior? We want to validate our client fanout logic.
- For the autoscale change, can you provide expected cost delta and any rollback plan?

If you can get an updated runbook with those items by Friday EOD, that meets our exec ask.

Chris
From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: Chris Barnes <chris@zephyrdata.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: 2027-01-21T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RCA (draft) — Zephyr us-west throughput/latency spike

Chris —

We’ve added the shard id trace dump and two example request payloads to the runbook (see remediation_runbook.xlsx, tab "Evidence"). Short summary in-line: the three hotspot shards were s-42, s-43, s-44; requests that fanout across those shards with >8 parallel segments amplified the head-of-line blocking on the controller.

Cost delta for autoscale smoothing change: projected +6–9% on Zephyr’s standby pool if left indefinitely; we propose a time-limited guard (30d) and an automated revert if 5xxs return to baseline. Rollback plan included in the runbook.

I’ll join your SRE call tomorrow at 09:00 PST to walk through the shard evidence and playbook steps.

Marcus Lin
Product Ops Lead, Redwood Dedicated
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Chris Barnes <chris@zephyrdata.com>, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: 2027-01-22T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Final RCA & commitment summary — Zephyr incident

Chris —

Thanks for the collaboration this week. Attached is the final RCA package (zephyr_rca_v1.pdf) and a locked remediation runbook with incremental sign‑offs (remediation_runbook.xlsx) plus the ownership matrix (ownership_matrix.csv). Highlights:
- Final owners and delivery dates: Rishi (autoscale + alerts) — 2027-01-25; Marcus (steady-state routing + standby pool) — 2027-01-21 (completed); Evelyn (leader-elect tests, regression evals) — 2027-02-02.
- Guardrails: 30d timeboxed autoscale smoothing window with automated revert; daily sentinel alerts for high-tail latency; weekly runbook drills with Zephyr SREs for 6 weeks.
- Follow-through: We will provide a weekly progress snapshot to Zephyr execs (Laura to own) and a public postmortem in 30 days if there are no regressions.

Next steps: Laura will set recurring 1:1 syncs for runbook verification; Marcus to confirm standby pool scaling is in steady state; Rishi to push autoscale change to canary on 2027-01-24.

Let us know if you want this packaged into a customer-facing one‑pager for your execs.

Best,

Laura Bennett
Customer Success Director
Redwood Inference
